Data Unit Samples: X-ray and Ledger Records

Four complete records from api.si.edu/openaccess/api/v1.0/content/<id>. Each includes an image, selected key fields, and an expandable view of the complete JSON. All four share the same three-layer structure: freetext (human-written labels and paragraphs), indexedStructured (controlled fields), and descriptiveNonRepeating (identifiers, links, and images).

Sample 1 · X-ray · Albatross North Pacific Expedition, 1906

Film: Conger erebennus (conger eel). The full 10,173 × 2,503-pixel strip is available to download as a TIFF/JPEG. The film bears a lead-letter marker reading USNM 163468 and the handwritten identifier RAD105688-001.

Scientific name
Conger erebennus,Anguilliformes › Congridae
Collection date
15 October 1906
Expedition / vessel
Albatross North Pacific Expedition, 1906;Vessel: Albatross
Station
D 5065 (Site Number in freetext.notes)
Location
Ose Saki, S. 57.5° E., 7.5 miles (Suruga Bay, Japan)
Coordinates
35.0944, 138.658(indexedStructured.geoLocation.points)
Depth
386–430 m ("Depth (m)" in physicalDescription)
Identifiers
USNM 163468;Tin Tag 4339;RAD105688
Notes
A curator’s investigation: the ledger lists station D.5063, but the date does not match. After consulting the tin tag ledger, the station was corrected to D.5065. The record itself documents how it was corrected.
License
Metadata: CC0; image: CC0
This record includes an exact date, station number, coordinates, and depth: all the information needed to place the X-ray along the expedition’s route. The “tin tag ledger” mentioned in the notes shows that the Division of Fishes also has its own ledger system, although its scans are not currently available through Open Access.

Sample 2 · X-ray · Albatross Philippine Expedition, 1907–1910

Film: Petroscirtes variabilis (a blenny). Two fish on one film, USNM 138268, RAD120244-001.

Scientific name
Petroscirtes variabilis,Blenniidae
Collection date
9 May 1908
Expedition / vessel
Albatross Philippine Expedition, 1907–1910;Vessel: Albatross
Location
Capunuypugan Point, Generale Island, Mindanao (east coast of Mindanao)
Coordinates
None (only a place hierarchy: North Pacific Ocean › Philippines › Locality)
Preparation
Polyester (the X-ray film material); preparation count: 1
Notes
“The collection date is incorrect. The Albatross was not in this area in 1909, but was at this location in 1908, so the date was corrected to 9 May 1908.”
As in Sample 1, the notes trace a curator’s use of voyage logs to reconstruct and correct the record. Both records show that the Albatross’s location on a given date provides the underlying structure of this dataset: the X-rays are tied to the expedition’s route. This record has no coordinates, however, revealing uneven coordinate coverage. Mapping it requires resolving place names to locations.

Sample 3 · Ledger · Division of Birds, Volume 30, Catalog Nos. 152076–152100 · Ridgway in Florida, 1896

Image ID: media:NMNH-vol.030_152076-152100. This page contains 25 rows documenting collections made by Robert Ridgway (the Smithsonian’s first curator of birds) in south-central Florida in 1895–1896. At the upper right, “Ex. Carnegie Mus., 1904” appears beside a Carolina parakeet entry.

Of the 25 rows, 21 have matching API records, all of which point back to the same page image, confirming the mapping in both directions. Of the four missing entries, 152093 is explicitly recorded in the ledger as having been exchanged to the Carnegie Museum in 1904. The ledger records departures; the database records current holdings. In addition, the five specimens numbered 152095–152099, Conuropsis carolinensis (Carolina parakeet), were collected at Taylor’s Creek on 29 February 1896. The species became extinct in 1918; this page captures a day in the final two decades of its wild population.

Sample 4 · Ledger · Division of Mammals, Catalog Nos. 573126–573150 · Philippine Fruit Bat, 1988

Image ID: media:NMNH-573126-573150 (Division of Mammals image IDs contain only the catalog number range, without a volume number).

Scientific name
Cynopterus luzoniensis (Luzon short-nosed fruit bat), Chiroptera › Pteropodidae; alternative name: C. brachyotis luzoniensis
Collection date
24 February 1988
Collector
R. B. Utzurrum; field number RBU 227
Location
Gigmoto, 1 km N, 8.5 km W, Buadan River, Catanduanes, Philippines; coordinates: 13.8, 124.32
Preparation
Skeleton;Skull;Female
Notes
GenBank submission and publication reference: Roberts 2006, Mol. Ecol. 15(8), on the phylogeography of Philippine fruit bats. This bat’s DNA is already in a public database.
USNM
573133;Accession 378386
Compare this with the 1896 bird ledger page: the same Government Printing Office form was still in use 92 years later, but the notes now point to GenBank and journal DOIs. A handwritten entry connects to a genetic sequence, illustrating the span of time that a “museum of ledgers” could explore.
